title: Comparison of preoperative transthoracic echocardiography by anesthesia versus cardiology regarding resulting consequences for perioperative planning and risk stratification in non-cardiac surgery patients
summary:
Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is regularly performed on patients in whom uncertainties about cardiac performance or heart valve functions have arisen during the anesthesia briefing discussion. If there are relevant impairments, an increased anesthesia risk is to be expected and this may also significantly change the procedure (e.g. selection of anesthesia procedure, monitoring in intensive care). A TTE is recommended in the guidelines if patients have...
1.) a new onset of shortness of breath of unknown cause,
2.) a worsening of symptoms of known heart failure within the last 12 months,
3.) a previously unknown or unexplained heart murmur.

However, delays and changes to the operation schedule often occur as a result of the additional processes between the disciplines involved (surgery - anesthesia - cardiology).

In addition to the TTE performed by a cardiologist, a simplified TTE is to be performed by anesthesiologists in the planned study. Then it will be examined whether the consequences derived from the two TTEs (e.g. choice of anesthesia method, date of operation) differ from each other. In addition, it will be checked whether the individual measured values ​​differ.
conditions: Heart valve disease, heart failure, pericardial effusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients who are regularly informed about anesthesia preoperatively
• Non-cardiac surgery patients for elective surgery or  
  Intervention with anesthesia
• Consent to participate in this study after providing detailed information 
  by an investigator
• At least one of the following criteria/symptoms is present:
– Newly occurring dyspnea of ​​unclear origin with reduced exercise capacity (< 4 metabolic equivalents or < 100 W) before planned surgery with medium or high risk of cardiovascular complications
– As yet unexplained worsening of symptoms of known heart failure in the last 12 months
– Previously unexplained or unknown heart murmurs before planned surgery with a medium or high risk of cardiovascular complications (even with normal exercise capacity)
– Patients with the above-mentioned symptoms/criteria without deterioration in the last 12 months but present TTE (maximum 12 months old)
Exclusion criteria:
• Lack of consent to participate in the study
• Pregnancy
• Cardiac surgery
• GUCH patients
• Urgent or emergency surgery
